## Introduction
This vignette contains information about using
[R Markdown](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/rmarkdown/) and
[**knitr**](https://yihui.org/knitr/).

An R Markdown file (`.Rmd`) is a plain-text file with R code and markup. The
markup is written in [markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/).
The R package [**rmarkdown**](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rmarkdown)
converts R Markdown files to an output file containing the R code, output of the
R code, and additional text.

- Converting an R Markdown file to an HTML file requires either
  [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org/) or
  [RStudio](https://posit.co/products/open-source/rstudio) that already includes
  `Pandoc`.
- Converting an R Markdown file to a PDF file requires a 
  [LaTeX](https://www.latex-project.org/get/) distribution, see the
  'R markdown cookbook' and the 'Definitive guide', both mentioned at
  [Documentation and help], for extensive help. Two common choices are 'MiKTex'
  and 'TinyTeX':
  
  - [MiKTex](https://miktex.org/): when installing MiKTex, set
    `install for all users` and `always install missing packages on the fly` for
    all users, see
    [this Stack Exchange post](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/27138/).
  - [TinyTeX](https://yihui.org/tinytex/): use the following code to set it up
    and see [here](https://yihui.org/tinytex/r/) for details:

```{r tinytex, eval = FALSE}
writeLines(c(
  '\\documentclass{article}',
  '\\begin{document}', 'Hello world!', '\\end{document}'
), 'test.tex')
tinytex::pdflatex('test.tex')
options(tinytex.verbose = FALSE)
```

## Global Settings for knitr used by R Markdown
For a list of available options, see `str(knitr::opts_chunk$get())` and the
overviews of [options](https://yihui.org/knitr/options/) and
[objects storing options](https://yihui.org/knitr/objects/) at the package
website.

The option `echo = FALSE` hides code from the output. Use numeric values to
include the code of particular chunks. To collect all code as an the appendix
at the end of of a document, see the section
[Put together all code in the appendix](https://pkg.yihui.org/rmarkdown-cookbook/code-appendix)
from the 'R markdown cookbook'.

If the option `include = FALSE` is used, code and results are **not** included
in the output but code **is** executed such that its results can be used in
other code chunks, which is useful as option for particular chunks, not as
global option.

If the option `error = TRUE` is used, code execution will **not** stop on error
(unless `include = FALSE`), but instead the error message is included in the
output. This is useful for non-interactive use in production settings. If the
option `error = FALSE` is used, code execution stops on error, which makes more
sense in interactive use during development of the script.

## Loading files
Files that have to be used by the R Markdown script (e.g., R scripts that are
sourced or data files that are read) should be placed in the same directory as
the `R Markdown` file, because by default the working directory when evaluating
R code chunks is the directory of the input document. The working directory can
be changed using `opts_knit$set(root.dir = ...)` but should **not** be changed
using `setwd()`, see the `Note` in `help("knit", package = "knitr")`.

## Knitting documents to HTML and PDF
The following lines can be used to `Knit` documents (i.e., generate output in
HTML or PDF files containing the script with its output and additional text)
containing a file name including a time-stamp. Using this way of creating
documents creates and keeps local R objects in the current environment. Although
that is useful for inspection and debugging, the potential use of local objects
can lead to non-reproducibility issues, such that the environment should be
cleared before using it and final files should be created by knitting (e.g.,
using the `Knit` button in RStudio), **not** by using `rmarkdown::render()`, see
[here](https://pkg.yihui.org/rmarkdown-book/compile.html#fnref2).

```{r render, eval = FALSE}
DateTimeStamp <- format(Sys.time(), format = "%Y_%m_%d_%H_%M")
rmarkdown::render("FilenameRMarkdownFile.Rmd", output_format = "html_document",
                  output_file = paste0("Filename", DateTimeStamp, ".html"),
                  output_dir = "./knitteddocs")
rmarkdown::render("FilenameRMarkdownFile.Rmd", output_format = "pdf_document",
                  output_file = paste0("Filename", DateTimeStamp, ".pdf"),
                  output_dir = "./knitteddocs")
```

## Adding and collecting code chuncks
Add a new chunk by either using the `Code` > `Insert Chunk` button or typing the
delimiters ```` ```{r} ```` above the code chunk and ```` ``` ```` below it.

To collect all chunks from a R Markdown document that contain R code into a
conventional R script use `knitr::purl("<filename>.Rmd", documentation = 0)`.
However, the various R Markdown options will **not** be incorporated in such an
R script, which might hamper exactly reproducing the analyses as executed when
running the R Markdown file, see the note in `help("purl", package = "knitr")`.

## Formatting in R Markdown

### Section headings and linking
Section headings can be created by putting a number sign (`#`) before the
heading text, with additional number signs creating sub-headings.

Links to another section in the same document can be created by putting the
section heading in square brackets: `[<Section title>]`. To show an alternative
text in the link, put the alternative text in square brackets before the section
heading: `[<link text>][<Section title>]`. To link to URLs, put the link text in
square brackets followed by the URL in round brackets:
`[<link text>](<vignette_filename>.html)`. If sections on the website are proper
headings, you can refer to them by adding a hash followed by the heading, with
spaces replaced by dashes (`-`).

```
This is a link to this section: [Formatting in R Markdown].
This is another link to the same section, with alternative text as link:
[The same section][Formatting in R Markdown].
And a link to the same section in
[the online version of this vignette](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/rmarkdown_knitr.html#formatting-in-r-markdown).
```
renders as:

This is a link to this section: [Formatting in R Markdown]. This is another link
to the same section, with alternative text as link:
[The same section][Formatting in R Markdown]. And a link to the same section in
[the online version of this vignette](https://jessealderliesten.github.io/develcoder/articles/rmarkdown_knitr.html#formatting-in-r-markdown).

### Italic, bold, strike through

````
*italic words*, _other italic words_, **bold words**, the combination of
_An **italic and bold phrase** in italic text_ and ~~strike through~~ all
emphasise part of a text
````
is rendered as:

*italic words*, _other italic words_, **bold words**, the combination of
_An **italic and bold phrase** in italic text_ and ~~strike through~~ all
emphasise part of a text

Partially bold text inside [link text][Section headings and linking] requires R
version 4.1.1 or later.

### Code chunks
R code chunks can be shown with or without its output through argument `eval`
(which is `TRUE` by default):

`````{r code-chunk-format, eval = FALSE}
```{r code-chunk-example}
sum(c(1, 2))
mean(c(1, 2))
```
`````
shows a code chunk with its output, like:
```{r code-chunk-example}
sum(c(1, 2))
mean(c(1, 2))
```

Whereas
`````{r code-chunk-format-no-output, eval = FALSE}
```{r code-chunk-example-no-output, eval = FALSE}
sum(c(1, 2))
mean(c(1, 2))
```
`````
shows a code chunk without its output, like:
```{r code-chunk-example-no-output, eval = FALSE}
sum(c(1, 2))
mean(c(1, 2))
```

### Table
````
| Name       | Description                      |
| :--------- | :--------------------------------|
| `Name one` | Some description                 |
| `Name two` | Some description                 |
````
gives:

| Name       | Description                      |
| :--------- | :--------------------------------|
| `Name one` | Some description                 |
| `Name two` | Some description                 |

### Lists
Lists need an empty line before the first item to be correctly rendered.
Sub-items are created by indenting them. Numbered lists (ordered lists) are
created by using a number followed by a dot (`1.`). Non-numbered lists
(non-ordered lists) are created by using asterisks (`*`), plus signs (`+`), or
dashes (`-`).

````
non-numbered list:

* item one
* item two
  * sub-item one
  * sub-item two

numbered list:

1. item one
2. item two

````
These lists are rendered as:

non-numbered list:

* item one
* item two
  * sub-item one
  * sub-item two

numbered list:

1. item one
2. item two

### Escaping
To include symbols that indicate markup as literal symbols, escape the starting
markup symbols with a backslash: `\*\*this is bold if not escaped**` renders as
\*\*this is bold if not escaped** , whereas `**this is bold if not escaped**`
renders as the bold **this is bold if not escaped**.

To include ``(`)`` in the **output**, escape them by enclosing with an
additional delimiters:  
for example, ``` `` `some text` `` ``` produces `` `some text` ``,
and ```` ``` `` `some text` `` ``` ```` produces ``` `` `some text` `` ```. Do
**not** start a line of code with a delimiter if you want to escape other
delimiters: that would be interpreted as starting a code section.

To include code to **create** code chunks (i.e., include code which escapes
chunk headings), use
````
r ''````{r use-sum}
1 + 2
```
````
to show how to create a code chunk like
```{r use-sum}
1 + 2
```

### Miscellaneous
Newlines can be forced using `\cr` or by ending a line with two spaces followed
by a newline.

Qoutes can be formatting by putting `>` in front of a line.

For an overview of mathematical notation see
https://rpruim.github.io/s341/S19/from-class/MathinRmd.html
